neighbours.label: the count argument of a Python .split(sep, ⟦n⟧) call that is indexed straight away: .split(':', ⟦1⟧)[0]

notes: Card: the top examples are mixed ('split(folder⟧)[1]', 'split(":", ⟦3⟧)[0]', '_TestClass(1⟦3⟧).square()', plus nouns just before a possessive: '3名⟦女孩⟧', 'l⟦adders⟧''); the output suppresses "'s", ")['", ')^', so it fires on the token just before a closing-and-continuing mark. Probes: one-line snippets scored 0.01-0.06; with context, split(':', 2)[0] 0.56 and split('@', 1)[1] 0.27; basename(folder) 0.01, Counter(12).double() 0.05, English possessives 0.08-0.10. So only the split-count case is claimed; this is a narrow slice of the pole.
